THE SOURCE OF TRUTH for navigator.webdriver. Three table rows at :395-397 map kEnableAutomation, kHeadless and kRemoteDebuggingPipe to EnableAutomationControlled(true). The feature has base_feature 'none' in runtime_enabled_features.json5:806, so this table and the block at :446 are the only production writers. Deleting the three rows and that block is the whole patch; nothing downstream needs touching, and the CDP override path in Navigator::webdriver keeps working for callers that deliberately ask for it.

Separate from the switch table and easy to miss. Enables AutomationControlled only when the port value parses to exactly 0, with an upstream comment explaining that an ephemeral port means ChromeDriver and a specific port means a human debugger. Puppeteer's default launch uses --remote-debugging-port=0, so this branch is the one that fires for the most common driver in the world.

Not a source: a two-line derivation over RuntimeEnabledFeatures::AutomationControlledEnabled() and probe::ApplyAutomationOverride. Patching here would satisfy a detector reading the property and would leave both inputs live for anything else that consults them.

The single include of the mixin declared in navigator_automation_information.idl:7-9. WorkerNavigator does not include it, which is why navigator.webdriver is undefined in worker scope and why a worker re-read is not a cross-check for this field. Recorded so that no patch adds the mixin to WorkerNavigator out of symmetry.

The CDP half of navigator.webdriver: 'enabled |= automation_override_.Get()'. Opt-in per session via Emulation.setAutomationOverride; no mainstream driver sends it. Left alone by the recommended patch.

Browser-side half of the same command. Note the side effect that is not in the command's name: enabling the override also creates an AutomationInfoBarDelegate (:156), so raising navigator.webdriver over CDP also shrinks the content area. Cleared in the handler destructor and on Emulation.disable (:126-131).

Gated on --dom-automation (content_switches.cc:277), not on --enable-automation, correcting two rows of resources/surfaces.json. When present it installs on the main world (dom_automation_controller.cc:41) and on every isolated world (:64-84), so the switch is all-or-nothing across realms.

Forwards kDomAutomationController and kEnableAutomation (:3874-3875) and kRemoteDebuggingPipe and kRemoteDebuggingPort (:3916-3917) into every renderer command line. This is why the AutomationControlled decision is made in the renderer rather than the browser, and it is the precedent subsystem 1 should read before deciding how profile data travels.

The startup 'Chrome is being controlled by automated test software' bar, shown whenever --enable-automation is present and bad-flags warnings are not disabled by policy. Message string IDS_CONTROLLED_BY_AUTOMATION, shared with the remote-server bar.

A third automation infobar, tracking live WebSocket connections. SCOPE: content/browser/devtools/devtools_http_handler.cc calls SetActiveWebSocketConnections only when mode_ == kWithApprovalOnly (:898, :1026, :405-409), which is the chrome://inspect opt-in server. A --remote-debugging-port server runs in kDefault mode and shows nothing, so the common automation path does not get this bar.

Disables infobar animations under --enable-automation, with the upstream reason that 'infobar animations cause viewport resizes' and are flaky for tests. The consequence for us is the inverse: under automation an infobar resizes the viewport in one step rather than over several frames, which a ResizeObserver can tell apart.

Returns false under --enable-automation before consulting --enable-auto-reload or --disable-auto-reload, so an automated browser never self-reloads a network error page. Observable to any site that can induce a load failure and watch.

Returns true unconditionally under --enable-automation or --test-type=webdriver, bypassing the user-interaction requirement for a payment handler. The upstream comment names chrome/test/chromedriver/chrome_launcher.cc as the reason. A merchant page can distinguish the two behaviours.

Creates window.chrome via content::GetOrCreateChromeObject and adds loadTimes and csi. Called unconditionally from ChromeRenderFrameObserver::DidCreateScriptContext (chrome_render_frame_observer.cc:393-397) for every world, and from ChromeContentRendererClient::WillEvaluateServiceWorkerOnWorkerThread (:1531-1534) for allowed service worker origins. So these two keys exist in main world, isolated worlds and service workers alike.

Decides which chrome.* keys a plain web page sees. chrome.app is exposed to all webpages and is explicitly excluded from the 'any feature available' test (:698-701); chrome.runtime is added only when CanWebpageContextConnectExternally - some extension names this URL in externally_connectable - or when some other web-available feature was exposed (:722-730). This is the source-side reason our T0 capture shows chrome.runtime absent, refuting the T2 claim that its absence is a headless tell.

Everything Runtime.enable does with page-side reach, in one function: beginEnsureAllContextsInGroup (:1129), setMaxCallStackSizeToCapture to the default (:1133), reportAllContexts, and a replay of buffered console messages to the new frontend (:1136-1155). Nothing here touches window or any web-exposed object.

Translates the V8 inspector callback into frame->GetSettings()->SetForceMainWorldInitialization(true). A Page Setting, not an inspector-local flag, which is why the effect outlives the inspector call and reaches the loader.

Consumes the setting: 'Forcibly instantiate WindowProxy, even if script is disabled.' Two further consumers at frame_loader.cc:1788-1793 and page.cc:1125-1135. The comment at :1786 that this 'breaks extensions abusing SetForceMainWorldInitialization and relying on the number of created window proxies' is upstream's own statement that the WindowProxy count is externally countable.

Runs on every console.* call with or without a frontend: stores a strong v8::Global per argument (:471-474) and stringifies each through V8ValueStringBuilder::toString (:483). So argument coercion and argument retention are stock behaviour, not CDP behaviour. V8ValueStringBuilder short-circuits a Proxy to '[object Proxy]' (:118-121) without touching a trap.

The attached-session-only path, and the reason the canonical CDP probe fails at this revision: it reads the own property descriptor first and returns an empty MaybeLocal when the descriptor carries a non-builtin get (:296-299), so defining a getter on an Error's own 'stack' does not get it called. Called from descriptionForError (:311-350) for name, stack and message. Note the fallbacks: a missing own descriptor, or a non-object descriptor, falls through to a plain object->Get, so an inherited accessor or a Proxy is a different question.

The one place where attaching a debugger changes global engine behaviour: on the transition to a non-null debug delegate it calls compilation_cache()->DisableScriptAndEval() and CollectSourcePositionsForAllBytecodeArrays, and sets is_active_, which is what gates every break. Triggered by Debugger.enable, not by session attach, and not by Runtime.enable.

What a `debugger` statement compiles to. Guards on break_points_active() - which defaults true (debug.cc:180) and is therefore not the real gate - then calls HandleDebugBreak, which returns immediately unless is_active() (debug.cc:2886). With no debug delegate the whole statement is a runtime call and a stack-guard check.
Where probe::ApplyUserAgentOverride reaches the main-thread user agent, and therefore the only scope that Emulation.setUserAgentOverride and Network.setUserAgentOverride reach directly.

Returns the stored user_agent_ with no probe. The value is a snapshot taken at construction - dedicated_worker.cc:561 passes execution_context->UserAgent(), threaded_worklet_messaging_proxy.cc:141 passes frame_client->UserAgent(). Contrast GetUserAgentMetadata() in the same class (worker_global_scope.cc:206-212), which DOES consult probe::ApplyUserAgentMetadataOverride, so userAgent and userAgentData in one worker can be made to disagree.

params->user_agent = browser_client->GetUserAgent(), in the BROWSER process. No renderer inspector probe is in this path, so no CDP user-agent override ever reaches ServiceWorkerGlobalScope. The decisive refutation of any CDP-based user agent spoof, and the reason the value must be set where the browser process computes it.

The only guard on the DevTools HTTP endpoint: reject when the Host header is present and is neither an IP literal nor a localhost name. No Origin check, no CORS header. A page fetching http://127.0.0.1:<port>/json sends an IP literal Host and passes the guard, so the cross-origin block comes from CORS and Local Network Access rather than from here.

Refuses to start any remote debugging transport when the default user data directory is in use, unconditionally under GOOGLE_CHROME_BRANDING and test-only otherwise. Whether Apostate builds Chrome-branded therefore decides whether --user-data-dir is mandatory for automation, which is a build decision with a product consequence.

Seeds every CDP-synthesised input event with blink::WebInputEvent::kFromDebugger (bit 23, web_input_event.h:138). No code under third_party/blink reads that bit, and it is not among the modifiers getModifierState exposes, so it is invisible to JavaScript. The events themselves take the normal input path and are trusted.

The gate: returns ScreenMacHeadless instead of ScreenMac whenever --headless is present. Real display hardware is never queried on a headless macOS launch, so no amount of correctness elsewhere recovers the true display.

Builds the entire display list from HeadlessScreenInfo values: label, color_depth, bounds, work_area_insets, device_pixel_ratio, rotation and is_internal. Reads --screen-info when present (:32-39) and otherwise a single default. This is where a profile-driven headless display would be injected, and the switch already carries every field needed.

bounds 800x600, work_area_insets zero, color_depth 24, device_pixel_ratio 1.0, is_internal false, empty label, rotation 0. The zero work-area insets are the structural tell: they make screen.availHeight == screen.height, which no macOS or Windows desktop produces. Shared by the macOS, Windows and Ozone headless screens.

The complete set of Blink features --headless changes: one entry, disabling blink::features::kPaintHolding. Worth watching across Chromium rolls - anything added to this block is by construction a headless-only behaviour difference, and the block is three lines long today.

Rewrites the command line before anything else starts: appends --incognito when neither --incognito nor --user-data-dir was given (:65-69), --no-error-dialogs and --no-first-run (:71-79), a unique temporary user data dir (:84-93), and on Linux --ozone-platform=headless (:97-99), --ozone-override-screen-size=800,600 (:100-104) and --use-angle=swiftshader-webgl (:108-113). Every one of those is a behaviour a page can eventually feel, and none of them was typed by the caller.

TransformProcessType(kProcessTransformToBackgroundApplication) in the browser process only. The process has no Dock icon, no menu bar and cannot present interactive windows, which is the OS-level cause of there being no NSWindow for RenderWidgetHostViewMac to find.

Defined as 'the in-process NSView exists and has no window'. Guards three separate compensations - Focus() at :1996-2007, OnFirstResponderChanged at :1980-1995, WasHidden at :663-671 and SetBounds at :679-688 - each added against a recent crbug. The compensation set is maintained reactively, so it should be treated as incomplete until a headless capture says otherwise.

enable_watchdog is false whenever --headless is present, on every platform, so a headless GPU process tolerates stalls a headed one kills. Paired with content/gpu/gpu_main.cc:299-310, which runs the GPU main thread on a different message pump under --headless - NS_RUNLOOP on macOS so CADisplayLink vsync still works, DEFAULT elsewhere, which changes frame cadence.
Installs a process-local in-memory clipboard before the platform one can be installed, whenever IsHeadlessMode(). Always empty at startup and never shares the user's real clipboard.

THE HOST READ, and it is an environment variable before it is a file. Line 1142 is `tzid = getenv("TZ")`; if that is a valid Olson ID (isValidOlsonID, line 1143) it is returned verbatim and nothing else is consulted. Only when TZ is unset or invalid does the code fall through to realpath/readlink of TZDEFAULT (/etc/localtime) at :1160-1194. On Windows the whole branch is replaced by uprv_detectWindowsTimeZone() at :1111, which reads the registry and has no TZ equivalent — so the env-var lever is POSIX-only and macOS and Windows need different mechanisms.

Wraps the host read: uprv_tzset(), uprv_tzname_clear_cache(), hostID = uprv_tzname(0) (:471), then createSystemTimeZone(hostStrID) (:493). The NAME comes from the host here; the OFFSETS and DST RULES do not — they are read out of icudtl.dat by createSystemTimeZone. Two different provenances in one object.

SOURCE OF TRUTH FOR THE DST RULE. openOlsonResource(id, ...) opens the zoneinfo64 resource inside icudtl.dat and builds an OlsonTimeZone from its trans/typeOffsets/typeMap vectors. Every offset a page can observe — getTimezoneOffset now, in January, in July, in 1970 — is a function of this table, not of the host. The host contributes the string only.

Returns DEFAULT_ZONE->clone() under gDefaultZoneMutex, initialising it once via umtx_initOnce(gDefaultZoneInitOnce, initDefault) — and initDefault (:545) returns immediately if DEFAULT_ZONE is already non-null, which is what makes an adoptDefault() issued before the first createDefault() stick. DEFAULT_ZONE is a single file-static per process (:602-614), so within one process no thread, no isolate and no worker can hold a different default from any other.

The single mutation point behind all three of Chromium's override layers. It writes the process-global DEFAULT_ZONE under gDefaultZoneMutex. This is the mechanical reason a worker cannot diverge from its parent WITHIN a process, and the reason divergence between processes is the only divergence that exists.

The filter that produces the exact count a detector reads. Three exclusions, in order: Etc/Unknown (:643), any id whose ZoneMeta::getCanonicalCLDRID differs from itself, i.e. every alias (:647-656), and any id whose region is "001" (:658-666). Applied to the 447 canonical entries in timezoneTypes.txt this leaves exactly 418 — see intl.supported-values, where the arithmetic is done.

SOURCE OF TRUTH FOR THE Intl LOCALE, and it is the C library's locale, not the browser's. It calls uprv_getPOSIXIDForDefaultLocale -> uprv_getPOSIXIDForCategory(LC_MESSAGES) (:1597), which is setlocale(LC_MESSAGES, nullptr), then getenv("LC_ALL"), then getenv("LC_MESSAGES"), then getenv("LANG"), and finally the literal "en_US_POSIX" (:1648) when all of them are "C", "POSIX" or absent. There is no CoreFoundation path: grepping the file for CFLocale returns nothing, so macOS's UI language is never consulted. Accept-Language is not consulted either, by anything, anywhere on this path.

THE ANSWER TO WHERE ICU DATA COMES FROM. LazyInitIcuDataFile (:138) resolves kIcuDataFileName = "icudtl.dat" (:93); on Apple platforms that is apple::PathForFrameworkBundleResource (:174), i.e. a file inside our own .framework bundle, never a host path. LoadIcuData mmaps it and hands the bytes to udata_setCommonData (:248), then udata_setFileAccess(UDATA_ONLY_PACKAGES) (:280) with the comment "Never try to load ICU data from files" — after this ICU is structurally incapable of reading host locale or tz data. The file itself is checked in at third_party/icu/common/icudtl.dat (10,876,560 bytes) and pinned by DEPS:2364 to chromium/deps/icu.git@d578f2e8b7bd5938e21cfb6bf15c079e0aa5b738.

Runs in EVERY process, browser and children alike, from content/app/content_main_runner_impl.cc:965 — see emit.content.main-runner-initialize-icu. Calls InitializeICUFromDataFile then DoCommonInitialization (:364), which calls InitializeIcuTimeZone (:368). This is the one function that exists in every process before any script runs, which makes it the natural single choke point for a process-uniform timezone.

DEAD ON OUR TARGETS. docs/SUBSYSTEMS.md §8 cites base/i18n/icu_util.cc:332 as the third override layer; at the pinned revision line 332 is `icu::TimeZone::adoptDefault(` inside `#if BUILDFLAG(IS_FUCHSIA)` (:321-333). The only other arm is `#elif BUILDFLAG(IS_CHROMEOS) || (IS_LINUX && !IS_CASTOS) || IS_ANDROID`, which merely warms the cache with createDefault(). On macOS and Windows the entire function body compiles to nothing. Patching line 332 changes nothing on any platform this project targets — but the function is still the right PLACE to add one, because it is reached from InitializeICU in every process.

The call is unconditional and outside any process_type check, so browser, renderer, GPU, network and utility processes all execute it. Only Android takes the sibling branch (:956-963) that inherits a file descriptor from the browser. This is why an ICU-level timezone or locale decision is automatically process-uniform, and a Blink-level one is not.

What actually decides the Intl locale on POSIX. setlocale(LC_ALL, "") makes the C library adopt the environment, and ICU then reads that back through setlocale(LC_MESSAGES, nullptr). Darwin's libc consults only LANG/LC_* — never CFPreferences — so a Finder-launched Chrome, which inherits no LANG, lands on "C" and therefore on en_US_POSIX, while the same binary started from a terminal with LANG=fr_FR.UTF-8 reports fr-FR. Note :263 immediately forces setlocale(LC_NUMERIC, "C"), so number formatting never follows the environment; only LC_MESSAGES/LC_CTYPE do.

The override that desktop Chrome does not use. Across the whole tree the non-test callers are android_webview, fuchsia_web, chrome/browser/ash, content/renderer/renderer_main.cc:174 (inside `#if BUILDFLAG(IS_CHROMEOS)`) and blink's DevTools LocaleController. On macOS, Windows and desktop Linux nothing calls it, so --lang and the browser UI language have no effect on Intl.

Compiled out on every platform we target: the whole block is inside `#if BUILDFLAG(IS_CHROMEOS)` (:166-180) and exists because the Chrome OS zygote starts before the browser knows the login locale. Recorded so the next reader does not mistake it for the desktop path.

THE BROWSER-SIDE AUTHORITY. `timezone_(icu::TimeZone::createDefault())` captures the browser process's ICU default at construction and keeps it as the value every renderer will be told. Everything downstream — AddClient, UpdateIcuAndNotifyClients, every renderer's TimeZoneController — is a copy of this member.

THE PROPAGATION MECHANISM, and it is push-on-bind rather than pull. The last statement is clients_.Get(id)->OnTimeZoneChange(GetTimeZoneId(*timezone_)) (:72): the moment a renderer binds, the browser sends it the zone unconditionally, without waiting for a change. So a renderer started after a zone change converges by the same path as one that was already running, and no separate at-launch plumbing is needed.

Line 51 is the browser's own icu::TimeZone::adoptDefault(new_zone.release()), immediately followed by NotifyClients (:53). Note the early return at :42-44 when *timezone_ == *new_zone: a change that compares equal is silently dropped, which matters if a patch tries to re-assert a zone the monitor already believes it has.

Subscribes to NSSystemTimeZoneDidChangeNotification and, on each one, calls UpdateIcuAndNotifyClients(DetectHostTimeZoneFromIcu()) (:25) — a fresh icu::TimeZone::detectHostTimeZone() (time_zone_monitor.cc:57-59). This is the re-detection path that will overwrite a patched zone if the user or the OS changes the system timezone mid-session, and it must be handled or the spoof silently reverts.

Called from core_initializer.cc:175 during renderer startup. Binds device.mojom.TimeZoneMonitor and calls AddClient, which is what triggers the browser's push. The reply is asynchronous, so between InitializeICU and that reply the renderer's ICU default is still its own host detection — a window that matters only if a patch fixes the browser and leaves ICU initialisation alone.

icu::TimeZone::createDefault() in the renderer, cached into host_timezone_id_ by the constructor (:100) unless kLazyBlinkTimezoneInit is enabled — and that feature is FEATURE_DISABLED_BY_DEFAULT (:41), so the eager read is the shipping behaviour. The value is kept so ClearTimeZoneOverride can restore it (:199). If the renderer's ICU default is the real host zone at this moment, the real zone is now resident in the renderer for the life of the process even after an override lands.

The line docs/SUBSYSTEMS.md cites, and it verifies exactly: :236 is icu::TimeZone::adoptDefault(timezone.release()). What follows is the part that matters for worker coherence: NotifyTimezoneChangeOnMainThread for every main-thread isolate (:239-245) and WorkerThread::CallOnAllWorkerThreads(&NotifyTimezoneChangeOnWorkerThread) (:246) for every live worker isolate. The ICU write is process-global and instantaneous; the V8 DateCache flush is per-isolate and is what this fan-out exists to deliver. A worker isolate that missed the flush would keep serving the old offset from its own cache even though ICU had already moved.

The mojo client end of the browser's push. Records the incoming id as host_timezone_id_ and then, only if no CDP override is in effect, applies it. This is the path a patched browser value travels to reach JavaScript, and it is the only one that is not CDP.

The ONLY caller of TimeZoneController::SetTimeZoneOverride in the entire tree outside its own header and tests. Emulation.setTimezoneOverride is therefore the sole production consumer of the Blink override layer. Forbidden to us by A1, and recorded so it is not mistaken for a supported internal API. Its bookkeeping is also a hazard in itself: SetTimeZoneOverride refuses a second override (:163-166) and skips the ICU write entirely when the requested zone canonically equals the host zone (:164), so a patch that sets the host zone first and then 'overrides' to the same value performs no write at all.

The locale mirror of the timezone controller, and it is CDP-only (Emulation.setLocaleOverride). Worth reading anyway because it documents the full flush a locale change requires and which a patch must reproduce: base::i18n::SetICUDefaultLocale, then per isolate LocaleConfigurationChangeNotification AND DateTimeConfigurationChangeNotification (:22-25), on every main-thread isolate and, via CallOnAllWorkerThreads (:78), every worker. Note the constructor caches icu::Locale::getDefault().getName() at :41, so the true host locale is retained in the renderer regardless.

`if (timezone_ == nullptr) timezone_ = icu::TimeZone::createDefault();` — one lazily cloned copy of the process-global default, held per isolate. Selected by Intl::CreateTimeZoneCache (:2828-2830) whenever v8_flags.icu_timezone_data, which is DEFINE_BOOL(icu_timezone_data, true) at v8/src/flags/flag-definitions.h:460, so this is the shipping cache and base::OS::CreateTimezoneCache is dead in a Chromium build.

Returns raw_offset + dst_offset from GetOffsets (:2789), which calls icu::TimeZone::getOffset for UTC input and BasicTimeZone::getOffsetFromLocal(UCAL_TZ_LOCAL_FORMER, UCAL_TZ_LOCAL_FORMER) for local input. Both read the OlsonTimeZone transition table, so getTimezoneOffset() at an arbitrary instant is a direct query against zoneinfo64 in icudtl.dat.

GetTimeZone()->getDisplayName(is_dst, icu::TimeZone::LONG, result) — the parenthetical in Date.prototype.toString. It is a LOCALISED display name pulled from the ICU default locale's zoneStrings bundle, and it is cached separately for the standard and daylight names. This is the one string that binds the timezone surface and the locale surface into a single token: "Indochina Time" is Asia/Bangkok rendered in en, and any other locale renders it differently.

A LANDMINE that is defused only by a default argument. On TimeZoneDetection::kRedetect this calls icu::TimeZone::adoptDefault(icu::TimeZone::detectHostTimeZone()) (:2825), i.e. it re-reads the host and discards any override. It is safe today because v8::Isolate::DateTimeConfigurationChangeNotification defaults to kSkip (v8/include/v8-isolate.h:1843-1844) and grepping the whole Chromium tree for kRedetect outside v8/ and third_party/node yields nothing. Any future embedder call with kRedetect silently reverts the spoof, so this belongs in the patch's regression test.

With icu_timezone_data on it forwards straight to tz_cache_->LocalTimeOffset (:207). The long historical-DST approximation that follows (:210-260) is the non-ICU fallback and is unreachable in a Chromium build.

Memoises the display name into tz_name_ / dst_tz_name_ (:98) per isolate; the memo is dropped by ResetDateCache (date.cc:42-60), which is exactly what DateTimeConfigurationChangeNotification triggers.

Assembles the string from three independently sourced parts: kShortWeekDays/kShortMonths, which are hard-coded English arrays and never localised; the numeric GMT+HHMM built from -date_cache->TimezoneOffset(time_ms) (:578-580); and local_timezone from DateCache::LocalTimezone (:581), which IS localised. So Date.prototype.toString mixes a fixed-English skeleton with a locale-sensitive zone name, and only the latter moves with the ICU locale.

Step 28.b.i of the spec, implemented as `tz.reset(icu::TimeZone::createDefault())` when the options bag names no timeZone. This is the single line that makes Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().timeZone a report of the process-global ICU default and nothing else.

CANONICALISES BEFORE REPORTING. tz.getID() is passed through icu::TimeZone::getCanonicalID (:615) and "GMT" is rewritten to "+00:00" (:611-612). So a patch that adopts an alias — Asia/Calcutta, US/Pacific, Etc/GMT-7 — will not see that alias come back out of resolvedOptions, and a check that compares the profile field against the reported string must compare canonical forms.
Pure assembly of the object a detector reads; every field it emits is sourced elsewhere. Included so the join from the observable to the real emitters is explicit rather than assumed.

Default-constructs an icu::Locale — which is icu::Locale::getDefault() — and caches it per isolate. Two rewrites happen here and nowhere else: "en_US_POSIX" and "c" both become the literal "en-US" (:8126-8130), and a bogus locale becomes "und". `return isolate->DefaultLocale();` — the spec's DefaultLocale() step, reached whenever the requested locale list is empty, which is exactly what `new Intl.NumberFormat()` and `new Intl.Collator()` do. One value therefore drives the locale field of every Intl constructor at once, which is why those three probes can never disagree with each other and why disagreeing with navigator.language is the interesting case.

FOURTEEN OF THE TWENTY PROBED VALUES ARE BUILD CONSTANTS. Each of these is now a one-line forward to LIBC_NAMESPACE::shared::<fn> (acos :80, asin :122, atan :164, atan2 :165, cos :167, exp :169, log :220, log1p :221, log2 :222, log10 :223, expm1 :225, cbrt :227, sin :229, tan :231) via #include "third_party/llvm-libc/src/shared/math.h" at :24. That header is source in our own checkout, pinned by DEPS:534 llvm_libc_revision 3ea89f4304312567e31a8eb45e0737577e65b676, compiled into the binary. The host's libm is not linked into any of these paths.

symbol: LIBC_NAMESPACE::math::sin (Ziv accuracy test and sin_accurate fallback)
notes: WHY THE BUILD CONSTANT IS ALSO ARCHITECTURE-INDEPENDENT, which is the non-obvious half. The fast path computes an error bound and runs Ziv's rounding test — `if (r_upper == r_lower) return r_upper;` (:215-219) — falling through to sin_accurate() when the two disagree, so the returned double is the correctly rounded one. LIBC_MATH_HAS_SKIP_ACCURATE_PASS, which would remove that fallback, is not defined anywhere in the Chromium or V8 build files. The FMA use at :93-106 is gated on LIBC_TARGET_CPU_HAS_FMA_DOUBLE, and cpu_features.h:103-105 defines that purely from compile-time predefines (__ARM_FEATURE_FMA, __AVX2__ && __FMA__) with NO runtime CPUID dispatch. Contrast emit.rust.fft-planner-cpu-dispatch in the audio shard, which dispatches on the host CPU at run time: this one cannot, and because the result is correctly rounded the FMA difference cannot change the answer anyway.

FIVE MORE BUILD CONSTANTS, by a different route: these are still the hand-ported fdlibm algorithms (acosh :95, asinh :134, atanh :186, cosh :247, sinh :306) and they are composed entirely out of the llvm-libc primitives above plus sqrt and fabs — e.g. asinh reaches log1p(|x| + t/(1+sqrt(1+t))). sqrt is the only non-llvm-libc ingredient and it lowers to the hardware square-root instruction, which IEEE-754 requires to be correctly rounded, so it introduces no host variance. Result: acosh, asinh, atanh, cosh and sinh are as build-determined as sin and exp.

THE FIRST OF TWO HOST FACTS, and it is one line at the very bottom of the file: `double tanh(double x) { return std::tanh(x); }`. Every sibling in this file was migrated to llvm-libc or kept as fdlibm; tanh alone was left calling <cmath>, so Math.tanh binds to Apple libm on macOS, glibc on Linux and UCRT on Windows. Structurally identical to the unqualified sin/exp calls the audio shard found in dynamics_compressor.cc:331,477 — the same class of oversight, in a surface detectors probe far more often.

THE SECOND HOST FACT, and the more surprising one because V8 still ships its own pow. Line 47-49 reads `if (v8_flags.use_std_math_pow) return std::pow(x, y);` and the flag is DEFINE_BOOL(use_std_math_pow, true) for every platform except AIX (v8/src/flags/flag-definitions.h:1229-1233). base::ieee754::legacy::pow — itself an llvm-libc forward at v8/src/base/ieee754.cc:300 — is therefore dead on all our targets. Math.pow(Math.PI, -100), which our collector probes, is an Apple-libm answer on a Mac. Note also the pre-dispatch special cases at :34-44: y==2 becomes x*x and y==0.5 becomes std::sqrt(x+0), so those two exponents are exact and host-independent while every other exponent is not.

The JIT's binding for the same functions: ieee754_sin_function -> base::ieee754::sin (:1198), ieee754_tanh_function -> base::ieee754::tanh (:1204), ieee754_pow_function -> math::pow (:1206). Compiled code therefore calls exactly what the interpreter calls, with pow honouring the same flag.

WHY THE VALUES ARE TIER-INDEPENDENT, which A3 needs. Constant folding calls the identical functions — base::ieee754::acos (:729) through base::ieee754::tanh (:886), and math::pow (:849). Turboshaft (turboshaft/machine-optimization-reducer.h:560,588) and Maglev (maglev/maglev-reducer-inl.h:3847,3994) also route pow through i::math::pow. So a value folded at compile time equals the value computed at run time, and repeatedly calling Math.sin cannot yield a different answer once the function tiers up.

Quantiser, not source, and the row that carries the granularity evidence. RoundRtt uses kGranularity = base::Milliseconds(50) with RoundToMultiple and a base::Seconds(3) cap; RoundMbps uses kBucketSize 50 kbps with kMaxDownlinkKbps = 10.0 * 1000. Both first multiply by GetRandomMultiplier(host) = 0.9 + (GetHash(host) + randomization_salt_) % 21 * 0.01, i.e. 0.90-1.10 per origin. 50 ms and 50 kbps, not the 25 the spec suggests, so a profile value is observable only at that granularity and only after the per-origin multiplier.

The source of the console-timing tell. Its fullStack=false branch decided how many frames every console API other than trace and timeEnd captures; upstream widened it from 1 to kDefaultMaxCallStackSizeToCapture whenever any session had V8RuntimeAgentImpl::enabled(). The walk runs on the calling thread, so the cost is charged to the page's own console call and grows with the page's call depth. Patched by 0087 to test V8DebuggerAgentImpl::enabled() instead, so the width tracks Debugger.enable rather than Runtime.enable.

Introduced by patch 0087. Holds the isolate's SetCaptureStackTraceForUncaughtExceptions decision, which upstream made inline in V8Debugger::setMaxCallStackSizeToCapture as soon as one front-end enabled the Runtime domain. That flag is the source of the throw-cost tell: V8 walks the live JS stack on the throwing thread, so try{throw 1}catch{} became depth-dependent. Now gated on the debug delegate and re-applied from V8Debugger::enable and V8Debugger::disable so a Debugger.enable arriving after Runtime.enable still turns it on. Keeps upstream's precondition that no enabled Runtime domain means no capture, so it only ever narrows.

Introduced by patch 0087. Called first from ServerWrapper::OnHttpRequest and ServerWrapper::OnWebSocketRequest; a true verdict closes the connection with ServerWrapper::Close rather than answering, because any HTTP response including an error resolves a no-cors fetch and tells the page the port is open. Keys on Origin and Sec-Fetch-Site, both forbidden header names. Allows Sec-Fetch-Site none (user-started navigation) and same-origin (the bundled front-end loading its own files), an Origin whose scheme is not http or https (chrome:// and devtools:// front-ends), an Origin equal to the endpoint's own authority (the front-end this endpoint serves), and the absence of both (every non-browser client, including Puppeteer and Playwright). Protects against a page, not against a process.

The single place Chromium configures V8's heap from installed memory, for every isolate in every process. Patched by 0087 to pass Profile::memory_total_bytes clamped to the host with std::min instead of base::SysInfo::AmountOfTotalPhysicalMemory, so V8's own arithmetic produces the ceiling and capacity is only ever reduced, matching the clamp in patches 0004 and 0006. This is a configuration change rather than an accessor override, so the reported limit is one the heap genuinely honours and cannot be falsified by allocation. Virtual memory stays the host's; it is not part of the claim.

Not the source, and not patched: it computes installed memory over 2 clamped to Heap::kDefaultMaxHeapSize of 4 GiB, and Heap::MaxReserved turns that into HeapStatistics::heap_size_limit. The clamp is why the readout saturates at 8 GiB of installed memory and why the contradiction with navigator.device-memory is invisible on a large host and live on a 2-4 GiB VM. Left alone deliberately so the mapping stays V8's own and cannot drift out of the value set a real Chrome produces.

Not the source, and not patched: it copies v8::HeapStatistics into HeapInfo, which serves BOTH performance.memory and console.memory through one MemoryInfo, so patching the configuration upstream covers both readouts. Precision differs between them: WindowPerformance::memory uses Precision::kPrecise when the process is locked to a site and kBucketized otherwise, MainThreadDebugger::memoryInfo is always kBucketized, and the thread-local HeapSizeCache is shared so a precise read poisons a later bucketized one for twenty minutes. Measured: 4395630592 bytes precise, 3760000000 bucketized, on a 36 GiB host.

Added by patch 0090, together with the fonts.enumeration_allowlist parse in base::apostate::Profile::ParseOrNull. THE SINGLE PREDICATE: the other four emitters call it and nothing else decides, which is why the four probe routes cannot disagree — there is no second copy of the matching rule to drift. fonts.local-src-lookup's existing note predicted the opposite failure ('a denylist installed there does NOT cover local(), so a subtractive patch applied at that one point leaves this oracle answering truthfully'); that prediction was correct and 0090 is built to satisfy it rather than repeat it.

The only two calls in Blink that hand a page-written family name to FontCache. Everything that measures or renders text by name converges here, including OffscreenCanvas and workers, because a Font owns a FontFallbackList whoever created it. Under 0090 a hidden family takes the branch an absent family already takes, so the next family in the list is tried and the page is never left without a font. Generic families are exempt by construction via FontFamily::FamilyIsGeneric().

What document.fonts.check() consults. blink::FontFaceSet::check returns true for any family the platform can match whatever the page's own @font-face rules say, so this is the function that makes check() a platform-availability oracle, and the one 0090 filters.

Also blink::LocalFontFaceSource::CreateFontData. local() matches a PostScript or full font name rather than a family name, so the allowlist cannot be consulted with the page's string — 'ArialMT' is Arial and no family list spells it that way. 0090 resolves the face and tests the family the platform actually produced, at BOTH entry points, because a source that reports unavailable and then renders is exactly the disagreement a probe wants.

The browser-side table behind queryLocalFonts(). The only place the table is built, and platform-independent, so one removal covers macOS, Windows and Linux. Nothing is ever added: an invented entry would carry a postscript name with no typeface behind it, and the next thing a page does with a FontData is measure it or call blob(). The existing emit.browser.font-enumeration-cache (GetFontEnumerationData) is the caller and stays as a waypoint.

Also gl::RealGLApi::glGetInteger64vFn and gl::RealGLApi::glGetFloatvFn. All three consult the single kApostateGlLimits table introduced by patch 0026 and extended by 0032, 0035, 0036 and 0070, which is why a limit cannot be served on one query path and leak on another. Reported by HonestyGaps. Patch 0119 changed what decides the value rather than the table: all six plain and robust entry points serve the composed claim when the CURRENT GL context is a WebGL-compatibility context, and the host's own value otherwise. The gate is RealGLApi::ApostateContextIsWebgl, which reads GL_ANGLE_webgl_compatibility off the driver's extension string through GLApiBase and caches it, one RealGLApi being constructed per gl::GLContext in GLContext::CreateGLApi. The gate cannot be the backend, and that is the blast radius worth recording: this is a GPU-process-wide function pointer, ui/gl/init/create_gr_gl_interface.cc binds Skia's get_integerv straight to it, and GrGLCaps reads MAX_SAMPLES, MAX_TEXTURE_SIZE and MAX_RENDERBUFFER_SIZE through it, so a claim served unconditionally would change raster and canvas2D rendering rather than a fingerprint.

NavigatorShare::ShareClientImpl::Callback already maps ShareError::CANCELED to the same kAbortError, so the exception NAME matched a genuine cancel and the message was the entire difference; 0094 calls ErrorToString for CANCELED rather than copying the literal, so the two cannot drift.

A waypoint rather than a source: the decision is base::apostate::Profile::FontFamilyEnumerable's.

The path that makes the surface deterministic without a network: a CDM placed in the preinstalled-component directory (<Framework>/Libraries/WidevineCdm on macOS) registers at startup for every profile. Measured first-call success at 30 ms on a fresh offline profile, macOS only.

INTRODUCED by patch 0100: substitutes the screen available rect when the real window rect has not arrived, so the bindings never hand script an empty rect. A waypoint by construction — it does not make the rect arrive, it stops the unarrived state being observable.

THE SOURCE. Reads the host's active keyboard layout and returns the DomCode -> character map navigator.keyboard.getLayoutMap() finally resolves with. Platform-specific: dom_keyboard_layout_map_mac.mm:72, dom_keyboard_layout_map_ozone.cc:67, dom_keyboard_layout_map_win.cc:154, all behind the same ui/events/keycodes/dom/dom_keyboard_layout_map.h declaration. `return ui::GenerateDomKeyboardLayoutMap();` verbatim. The aura view (render_widget_host_view_aura.cc:1537) forwards to its host window instead, so the per-platform view is the join between the ui/ generator and the content/ chain.

THE OVERRIDE SITE, patch 0021. Not the source of truth in stock Chromium - it relays the widget host - but it is the only path by which a layout reaches a renderer, because KeyboardLockServiceImpl reads it here and nowhere else, so replacing the map here covers the accessor without touching it.
